items.title: Tempered time-ordered scalar two-point carrier
items.design_state: Planned tempered scalar time-ordered carrier with fixed local Fourier and metric conventions; conditional distributional construction and Green-source proof authored.
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Fix the scalar shell parameter $\mu\ge0$ and all shell, Fourier, and metric conventions of [[def-qft-scalar-mass-shell]], with $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$ and $\Box=-\partial_t^2+\Delta_{\mathbf x}$. For $\phi\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^4)$ define the partial spatial Fourier transform
$$\widehat\phi_t(\mathbf k)=\int_{\mathbb R^3}e^{-i\mathbf k\cdot\mathbf x}\phi(t,\mathbf x)\,d^3\mathbf x$$
and define $H_\mu\in\mathcal S'(\mathbb R^4)$ by
$$\langle H_\mu,\phi\rangle=\int_{\mathbb R}dt\int_{\mathbb R^3}\frac{d^3\mathbf k}{(2\pi)^3\,2\omega_\mu(\mathbf k)}e^{-i\omega_\mu(\mathbf k)|t|}\widehat\phi_t(-\mathbf k).$$
This is a continuous distributional extension of the free scalar time-ordered two-point function: on $t>0$ its kernel is the Wightman two-point distribution $W_\mu(t,\mathbf x)$, and on $t<0$ it is $W_\mu(-t,-\mathbf x)$. The displayed partial Fourier formula fixes the extension at $t=0$; no product of a step function with an unspecified singular distribution is used. The kernel is symmetric under $(t,\mathbf x)\mapsto(-t,-\mathbf x)$, agrees with the two orderings on spacelike-separated supports, and obeys
$$ (\Box-\mu^2)H_\mu=i\delta_0 $$
in $\mathcal S'(\mathbb R^4)$. There is no extra prefactor $i$ in the definition of $H_\mu$.

items.title: Classical free action variations and normalization
items.design_state: Planned compact-variation scalar and commuting-spinor action equations; both directions authored.
items.statement:
Fix $\mu\ge0$, $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, $\Box=\eta^{ab}\partial_a\partial_b$, and the Dirac matrices and adjoint of [[def-qft-dirac-projections]]; $\mu$ is the inverse-length mathematical shell parameter of [[def-qft-scalar-mass-shell]]. For a smooth real scalar field $\phi$ and smooth commuting complex spinor $\psi:\mathbb R^4\to\mathbb C^4$, use the normalized free Lagrangian densities
$$\mathcal L_\phi=-\frac12\left(\eta^{ab}\partial_a\phi\,\partial_b\phi+\mu^2\phi^2\right),\qquad \mathcal L_D=\bar\psi\left(i\gamma^a\partial_a-\mu\right)\psi,\qquad \bar\psi=\psi^\dagger\beta.$$
For compactly supported smooth real variations $h$ and compactly supported smooth complex spinor variations $\chi$, the action symbols are used only through the following finite, compactly supported first variations; no global integrability of the background fields is assumed:
$$\delta S_\phi(\phi;h)=\int_{\mathbb R^4}h(\Box-\mu^2)\phi\,d^4x,\qquad \delta S_D(\psi;\chi)=2\operatorname{Re}\int_{\mathbb R^4}\chi^\dagger\beta\left(i\gamma^a\partial_a-\mu\right)\psi\,d^4x.$$
Each field is stationary under all such variations if and only if its corresponding Euler–Lagrange equation holds pointwise:
$$(\Box-\mu^2)\phi=0,\qquad (i\gamma^a\partial_a-\mu)\psi=0.$$
The adjoint Dirac equation follows from the second equation because the fixed matrices satisfy $(\gamma^a)^\dagger\beta=\beta\gamma^a$. These are mathematical variation identities for commuting classical fields; they assert no quantization, Grassmann calculus, or physical measurement.

items.title: Domain-qualified free observables and point-field obstruction
items.design_state: Planned free-field domains, moments and compositions, with representation-specific point-smearing obstructions authored.
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice and use the scalar and Dirac free-field constructions of [[lem-qft-smeared-free-scalar]] and [[lem-qft-free-dirac-car-locality]] with their current draft hypotheses, including the Dirac projection and CAR inputs in [[lem-qft-dirac-projection-matrices]] and [[lem-qft-fock-ccr-car]]. For a real scalar test $f\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^4)$, $\overline{\Phi_\mu(f)}=\sqrt2\,\Phi_{\rm Segal}(K_\mu f)$ is self-adjoint on the exact domain given by [[lem-qft-segal-weyl-domain]]. On scalar bosonic Fock space, $N_s=d\Gamma(1)$, $H_s=d\Gamma(\omega_\mu)$, and $P_{s,j}=d\Gamma(-k_j)$ are the maximal real multipliers of [[lem-qft-second-quantized-spectrum]]; in particular,
$$D(N_s)=\left\{\Psi=(\Psi_n):\sum_{n\ge1}n^2\|\Psi_n\|^2<\infty\right\},$$
and the Hamiltonian and momentum domains are exactly the square-integrability domains of the sums of their one-particle multipliers.

On the specified Dirac Fock space, spacetime-smeared fields $\Psi(F)$ are bounded, while the translation generators $H_D,P_{D,j}$ have the exact maximal domains and joint PVM stated in [[lem-qft-dirac-fermionic-translation-spectrum]]. For any one of these self-adjoint real-multiplier operators $A$, a normalized $\Psi\in D(A)$ has finite mean $\langle\Psi,A\Psi\rangle$ and finite variance
$$\operatorname{Var}_\Psi(A)=\|(A-\langle\Psi,A\Psi\rangle)\Psi\|^2.$$
Membership in $D(A)$ suffices for finite variance and does not require $\Psi\in D(A^2)$. A product $AB\Psi$ is defined only when $\Psi\in D(B)$ and $B\Psi\in D(A)$, as specified in [[lem-nrqm-uncertainty-schrodinger-robertson-anticommutator-bound]].

For the scalar point limit, fix $x_0\in\mathbb R^4$ and real tests $f_\varepsilon\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^4)$, $0<\varepsilon\le1$, such that $\int f_\varepsilon(x)\phi(x)\,d^4x\to\phi(x_0)$ for every Schwartz test $\phi$ and $K_\mu f_\varepsilon(p)\to e^{ip\circ x_0}$ for $\nu_\mu$-almost every shell momentum. Then $\|\Phi_\mu(f_\varepsilon)\Omega\|\to\infty$. A sufficient condition for both convergences is $\int f_\varepsilon=1$, $\sup_\varepsilon\|f_\varepsilon\|_1<\infty$, and $\int_{|x-x_0|\ge\delta}|f_\varepsilon(x)|\,d^4x\to0$ for each $\delta>0$. This includes all nonnegative normalized Schwartz approximate identities with mass concentrating at $x_0$, as well as signed families satisfying that condition; weak distributional convergence alone is not substituted for convergence of the mass-shell Fourier restriction. For the equal-time Dirac CAR field, fix $\mathbf x_0\in\mathbb R^3$ and $z_0\in\mathbb C^4\setminus\{0\}$. For every family $u_\varepsilon\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C^4)$ satisfying $\int h(\mathbf x)^\dagger u_\varepsilon(\mathbf x)\,d^3\mathbf x\to h(\mathbf x_0)^\dagger z_0$ for each spinor Schwartz test $h$, the bounded equal-time smeared operators satisfy $\|\Psi_t(u_\varepsilon)\|_{\rm op}\to\infty$ at each fixed time $t$. Thus neither construction gives a point-field value in the indicated norm topology. The supplied free-field results define only smeared fields and do not define coincident diagonal products.

references.title: Mark Srednicki, Quantum Field Theory, author-hosted 2006 prepublication book draft, §§3, 8, and 36
references.locator: Complete 616-page draft; §3 canonical scalar mode expansion, §8 free propagator, and §36 spinor-field Lagrangian. The spinor discussion uses anticommuting fields. Its formal field notation is contextual; exact domains and point-limit conclusions below follow from the stated Fock suppliers and local norm arguments.

items.proof:
**Given:** [A1] and [F1]–[F18].

1.1 The measure $d\nu_\mu$ is sigma-finite by [F9], and $\omega_\mu$ and $k_j$ are finite measurable multipliers by [F2]. Applying [F5] with one-particle multiplier vector $(1,\omega_\mu,-k_1,-k_2,-k_3)$ gives the self-adjoint scalar operators $N_s,H_s,P_{s,j}$. On sector $n$, their multipliers are $n$, $\sum_{r=1}^n\omega_\mu(\mathbf k_r)$, and $-\sum_{r=1}^n k_{r,j}$. Squaring these multipliers and integrating against the completed product measure yields exactly the stated domains. [A1, F1, F2, F5, F9, given]

1.2 The Dirac data in [F6] satisfy the measurable, finite-multiplier hypotheses of [F7], and [F16] supplies the complementary orthogonal projections and closed ranges required by that carrier. The one-particle measure is sigma-finite: each of the two species copies of R^3 is the countable union of bounded balls with finite Lebesgue measure. Let Y_m be the two species copies restricted to the ball of radius m; each Y_m has finite measure. For fixed n, the product sets Y_m^n have finite product measure and cover X^n as m grows. Their countable union over n and m is a sigma-finite cover of the Fock direct-sum measure. The particle and antiparticle sector multipliers are therefore self-adjoint on the maximal domains in [F7], which are the displayed square-integrability conditions for $H_D$ and each $P_{D,j}$. The field boundedness and equal-time CAR are exactly the inspected interfaces in [F8]. [A1, F1, F6, F7, F8, F16, given]

2.1 For real $f$, [F3] identifies the scalar field on $\mathcal D_{\rm fin}$ with $\sqrt2\,\Phi_{\rm Segal}(K_\mu f)$. The Hilbert space $H_\mu$ is separable by [F13], so the hypothesis of the Segal-domain result [F4] holds. Multiplication by the nonzero scalar $\sqrt2$ does not change an operator domain; hence the closure is self-adjoint on the domain in [F4] with $h=K_\mu f$. If $K_\mu f=0$, both operators are zero on all Fock space. [F1, F3, F4, F13, step 1.1, algebra]

2.2 For a normalized $\Psi\in D(A)$, Cauchy–Schwarz [F12] gives $|\langle\Psi,A\Psi\rangle|\le\|A\Psi\|<\infty$. Since $A$ is self-adjoint, this expectation is real. The vector $A\Psi-\langle A\rangle_\Psi\Psi$ belongs to the Hilbert space because both terms do, so its norm and the stated variance are finite without requiring $\Psi\in D(A^2)$. By [F14], a product $AB$ acts only on vectors $\Psi\in D(B)$ for which $B\Psi\in D(A)$; it is not defined merely because both $A$ and $B$ separately exist on a common dense core. [F1, F12, F14, step 1.1, step 1.2, given]

2.3 Choose $b_d$ from [F18] for $d=3,4$. Put
$Z_d=\int b_d(x)\,d^dx$ and $\rho_d=Z_d^{-1}b_d$.
The integral is finite because $0\le b_d\le1$ and its support lies in a
bounded ball, and it is positive because $b_d=1$ on a ball of positive
volume. Every derivative of $b_d$ is continuous with compact support, so
all its coordinate-weighted derivatives are bounded. Thus $\rho_d$ is
Schwartz, nonnegative, nonzero, and has integral one. In particular
$0<\|\rho_d\|_2<\infty$. Define
$\widehat\rho_d(\xi)=\int e^{-i\xi\cdot x}\rho_d(x)\,d^dx$.
The integral triangle inequality gives $|\widehat\rho_d(\xi)|\le\int\rho_d=1$;
dominated convergence [F10], with majorant $\rho_d$, gives
$\widehat\rho_d(\xi)\to1$ as $\xi\to0$.
Set $\rho=\rho_4$ and, for $\varepsilon>0$, define $\rho_{\varepsilon,x_0}(x)=\varepsilon^{-4}\rho_4((x-x_0)/\varepsilon)$. For every Schwartz test $\phi$, change of variables and dominated convergence [F10], with majorant $\|\phi\|_\infty\rho_4(y)$, give $\int\rho_{\varepsilon,x_0}(x)\phi(x)\,d^4x\to\phi(x_0)$, so this is a point-mass approximation. For $p=(p^0,\mathbf p)\in H_\mu^+$ the same change of variables gives
$$K_\mu\rho_{\varepsilon,x_0}(p)=e^{ip\circ x_0}\widehat\rho_4\bigl(\varepsilon(-p^0,\mathbf p)\bigr).$$
Thus $K_\mu\rho_{\varepsilon,x_0}(p)\to e^{ip\circ x_0}$ for every fixed shell momentum and $|K_\mu\rho_{\varepsilon,x_0}(p)|\le1$. The shell measure has infinite total mass: in radial coordinates, for $r\ge\max(1,\mu)$, $\omega_\mu(r)\le\sqrt2\,r$, so its radial density is bounded below by a positive constant times $r\,dr$, whose integral diverges. Fatou's lemma [F11] therefore gives $\liminf_{\varepsilon_m\downarrow0}\|K_\mu\rho_{\varepsilon_m,x_0}\|^2\ge\int_{H_\mu^+}1\,d\nu_\mu=\infty$. By [F1, F3] and the creation formula on the vacuum, $\|\Phi_\mu(\rho_{\varepsilon_m,x_0})\Omega\|=\|K_\mu\rho_{\varepsilon_m,x_0}\|$, so these vacuum vectors have no finite-norm point-field limit. More generally, suppose $f_\varepsilon$ satisfies the scalar hypotheses in the Statement. For any sequence $\varepsilon_j\to0$, Fatou [F11] applied to $|K_\mu f_{\varepsilon_j}|^2$ gives $\liminf_j\|K_\mu f_{\varepsilon_j}\|^2\ge\int1\,d\nu_\mu=\infty$. Thus the norms diverge as $\varepsilon\to0$: otherwise a bounded sequence with $\varepsilon_j<1/j$ could be selected using [A1], contradicting this conclusion. The vacuum creation identity gives the asserted field-vector norm. To verify the sufficient concentration condition, let $M=\sup_\varepsilon\|f_\varepsilon\|_1$ and let $g$ be any bounded continuous scalar function. Since $\int f_\varepsilon=1$, splitting the integral at radius $\delta$ gives $|\int f_\varepsilon(x)g(x)\,d^4x-g(x_0)|\le M\sup_{|x-x_0|<\delta}|g(x)-g(x_0)|+2\|g\|_\infty\int_{|x-x_0|\ge\delta}|f_\varepsilon(x)|\,d^4x$. First choose $\delta$ using continuity at $x_0$, then take $\varepsilon\to0$. Applying this to Schwartz $g$ and to $g(x)=e^{ip\circ x}$ proves both required limits. Every rescaling of a nonnegative normalized Schwartz profile has $M=1$ and satisfies concentration by its integrable tail; hence the general conclusion includes every such profile, not only the chosen bumps. [A1, F1, F2, F3, F9, F10, F11, F18, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 The scalar one-particle space contains a unit vector $e$, for example a normalized indicator of an annulus $1<|\mathbf k|<2$, whose shell measure is finite and positive by [F2]. The symmetric vectors $e^{\otimes n}$ are unit vectors in mutually orthogonal sectors. Put $C=(\sum_{n\ge1}n^{-4})^{-1/2}$ and $\Psi_n=Cn^{-2}e^{\otimes n}$. By [F15], $\sum n^{-4}$ converges and is positive, so $C$ is well-defined and $\Psi$ is normalized. Also by [F15], $\sum n^{-2}<\infty$, so $\Psi\in D(N_s)$ and $N_s\Psi=(Cn^{-1}e^{\otimes n})_{n\ge1}$ is a Fock vector. Its image under one more application of $N_s$ would have squared norm $C^2\sum_{n\ge1}1=\infty$, so $N_s\Psi\notin D(N_s)$. By the composition-domain rule [F14] with $A=B=N_s$, $\Psi\notin D(N_s^2)$. Its mean and variance are finite by 2.2. [F1, F2, F5, F14, F15, step 2.2, construct, algebra]

4.1 Fix a unit spinor $z\in\mathbb C^4$ and, for $\varepsilon>0$, define $u_\varepsilon(\mathbf x)=\varepsilon^{-3}\rho_3((\mathbf x-\mathbf x_0)/\varepsilon)z$. For every spatial Schwartz test, change of variables and [F10] show that its pairing with $u_\varepsilon$ tends to the test's value at $\mathbf x_0$ times $z$, while $\|u_\varepsilon\|_2=\varepsilon^{-3/2}\|\rho_3\|_2\to\infty$. For a general family in the Dirac Statement, set $e=z_0/\|z_0\|$ and $h_a(\mathbf x)=b_3((\mathbf x-\mathbf x_0)/a)e$ for $a>0$. By [F18], this is a spinor Schwartz test, $h_a(\mathbf x_0)^\dagger z_0=\|z_0\|$, and $\|h_a\|_2=a^{3/2}\|b_3\|_2$. Given $L>0$, choose $a$ with $\|h_a\|_2<\|z_0\|/(2L)$. The assumed pairing limit then gives $|\langle h_a,u_\varepsilon\rangle_2|>\|z_0\|/2$ for all sufficiently small $\varepsilon$. Cauchy–Schwarz [F12] implies $\|u_\varepsilon\|_2>L$. Thus every such family has $\|u_\varepsilon\|_2\to\infty$. The following operator estimate applies to either the explicit bump family or this arbitrary family. By [F16], choose countable dense sets in the two Dirac energy ranges. Conjugating the negative-range dense set preserves density, and the Cartesian product of the two dense sets is countable and dense in the Hilbert direct sum. Therefore the one-particle space for the CAR Fock representation is separable and [F17] applies. For $A_\varepsilon=\Psi_t(u_\varepsilon)$, [F8] gives $A_\varepsilon A_\varepsilon^\dagger+A_\varepsilon^\dagger A_\varepsilon=\|u_\varepsilon\|_2^2I$. By [F17], the creation and annihilation terms are bounded, hence so is their sum. Cauchy–Schwarz [F12] gives $\sup_{\|x\|=\|y\|=1}|\langle A_\varepsilon x,y\rangle|\le\|A_\varepsilon\|$, while choosing $y=A_\varepsilon x/\|A_\varepsilon x\|$ for each unit $x$ with $A_\varepsilon x\ne0$ gives equality after taking the supremum over $x$. The adjoint identity swaps $x$ and $y$, so the same two-vector supremum equals $\|A_\varepsilon^\dagger\|$. For bounded operators $X,Y$, each unit $\xi$ satisfies $\|XY\xi\|\le\|X\|\,\|Y\xi\|\le\|X\|\,\|Y\|$ and $\|(X+Y)\xi\|\le\|X\xi\|+\|Y\xi\|\le\|X\|+\|Y\|$; taking suprema gives product submultiplicativity and the triangle inequality. Applying these inequalities to the CAR identity yields $\|u_\varepsilon\|_2^2=\|A_\varepsilon A_\varepsilon^\dagger+A_\varepsilon^\dagger A_\varepsilon\|\le2\|A_\varepsilon\|^2$. Thus $\|A_\varepsilon\|\ge\|u_\varepsilon\|_2/\sqrt2\to\infty$, excluding a bounded equal-time point-field norm limit. [F8, F10, F12, F16, F17, F18, step 2.3, given, algebra] ∎

items.title: Timeordered derivative jump gives iδ Green source
items.design_state: Planned mode derivative-jump verification; complete half-line distributional proof authored.
items.statement:
Let $\mu\ge0$, $\omega_\mu(\mathbf k)=\sqrt{|\mathbf k|^2+\mu^2}$, and for a fixed $\mathbf k$ with $\omega_\mu(\mathbf k)>0$ set
$$g_{\omega_\mu}(t)=\frac{e^{-i\omega_\mu(\mathbf k)|t|}}{2\omega_\mu(\mathbf k)}.$$
This is the time-mode factor of the tempered scalar carrier in [[lem-qft-free-time-ordered-kernel]]. Its first derivative has jump $-i$ at $t=0$, giving the Green source $i\delta_0$ after applying the $(-,+,+,+)$ Klein–Gordon operator and Fourier-inverting the spatial momentum.
